text:
Zoe: Quick follow-up from the all-hands re: regional GPU shortages and autoscaler behavior. Dropping the quick Qs and proposals here.
Raj: Thanks Zoe. first: who flips traffic to burst pools?
Priya: SRE oncall makes the call; infra runs the routing change. we have automated alerts but oncall confirms.
Mei: Are there hard thresholds we can publish? customers want predictability.
Priya: Proposal: reserved GPU >= 90% for 4m AND queue growth > 25% over 10m. requires two consecutive windows.
Zoe: What about Dedicated customers?
Priya: Dedicated default: auto-failover disabled. tenant setting: tenant_controls.allow_failover (bool).
Raj: Sequence of fallbacks?
Priya: 1) lower-power GPU profile, 2) increased batching window, 3) CPU-only for batch/embeddings, 4) rate limit. chat is excluded from cpu fallback by default.
Mei: Canary plan for quality: 3% traffic for 10m; abort if resp_quality_drop > 8% or latency +25%.
infra-bot: Canary started: fallback-canary -> cpu-variant (us-east-1) at 2026-07-01T14:00:00Z. metrics streaming OK.
Zoe: Communications: banner in console + targeted email + auto support ticket. legal will review copy for regulated customers.
Raj: Action items: Priya -> add thresholds to runbook; Mei -> add canary abort metrics; Zoe -> draft comms; infra-bot -> schedule a staging dry-run.
Priya: I will update runbook today.
Mei: I will add quality hooks to evals dashboard.
Zoe: Thanks all. we should rehearse this in the next ops drill.
__notes: All-hands follow-up: short thread with thresholds, tenant opt-out, fallback sequence, canary rules, comms, and action items for GPU supply/auto-failover
